claim: ACLs can be disabled on new and existing buckets. On an existing bucket with objects, after ACLs are disabled the bucket and object ACLs no longer take part in access evaluation and access is decided by policies; ACLs can be re-enabled later and the earlier ACLs come back.
question: What happens to existing object ACLs when you disable ACLs on a bucket?

values.display: the object and bucket ACLs are no longer part of an access evaluation
your preexisting bucket and object ACLs are restored

evidence.quote: In the case of an existing bucket that already has objects in it, after you disable ACLs, the object and bucket ACLs are no longer part of an access evaluation, and access is granted or denied on the basis of policies. For existing buckets, you can re-enable ACLs at any time after you disable them, and your preexisting bucket and object ACLs are restored.

claim: A directory bucket in an Availability Zone with no request activity for at least 90 days becomes inactive and is temporarily unreadable and unwritable; it keeps all data and metadata, storage charges continue, and an access request reactivates it, typically within a few minutes, with HTTP 503 errors during the transition.
question: What happens to a directory bucket that is not used for a long time?

values.display: inactive buckets retain all storage, object metadata, and bucket metadata
reads and writes return an HTTP 503 (Service Unavailable) error code

qualifiers.condition: no request activity for at least 90 days; does not apply to Local Zone buckets

evidence.quote: Directory buckets in Availability Zones that have no request activity for a period of at least 90 days transition to an inactive state. While in an inactive state, a directory bucket is temporarily inaccessible for reads and writes. Inactive buckets retain all storage, object metadata, and bucket metadata. Existing storage charges apply to inactive buckets.

If you make an access request to an inactive bucket, the bucket transitions to an active state, typically within a few minutes. During this transition period, reads and writes return an HTTP `503 (Service Unavailable)` error code. This doesn't apply to buckets in Local Zones.
